author: e. r. bennett
title: Houston Baptist University boosts women's basketball spending by 5.4% above Texas average in 2024
text:
Houston Baptist University in Texas allocated $1,208,253 to its women’s basketball teams in 2024, exceeding the state average of $940,344 by $267,909, according to the U.S. Department of Education .
This amount represented 6% of the university’s total athletics budget during 2024.
Houston Baptist University’s spending on sports programs has grown by 147% since 2010.
Basketball ranks among the top college sports in the United States , along with football, as premier NCAA programs attract substantial fan support and TV audiences comparable to those of the NBA. Events like March Madness capture millions of viewers annually.
The college sports landscape has shifted after a federal settlement enabled schools to share revenue directly with athletes for the first time. The settlement also compels the NCAA to distribute $2.8 billion in back damages over 10 years to athletes competing from 2016 onward.
In 2022, following extended legal and legislative action, athletes secured the right to benefit from their names, images and likenesses under new state laws and a change in NCAA policy.
The NCAA earned approximately $900 million in revenue during fiscal year 2024 from March Madness and related Division I men’s basketball tournament media rights, making basketball its most significant revenue source.
